newsitem.title: BELGIUM: EU approves Italian EMU tax plans.
newsitem.headline: EU approves Italian EMU tax plans.

text.p: The European Union ruled on Friday that Italy's proposed euro-tax meets EU accounting rules and may be used to reduce its 1997 budget deficit and help Rome qualify for the single currency.
"Eurostat has decided that the Italian tax on wage funds is a new tax and should be recorded as a receipt reducing the deficit," the EU's statistical organisation said in a statement.
Italy, like other EU states, is trying to bring its deficit, debt and other budget targets into line with criteria set in the EU's Maastricht treaty for qualifying for the EU's single currency.

In Rome, the Italian Treasury welcomed the decision, but the German finance ministry, where there is concern about Italy's fitness to be a founding member of the new euro currency, declined to comment.
Eurostat estimated that the part of the so-called euro-tax it was reviewing would represent 0.19 percent of GDP.

The estimated amount to be collected under that portion of the tax is 3.5 trillion lire, the office added. This is less than the 5.5 trillion lire analysts had originally anticipated would be covered under the ruling.

European Commission officials stresed that the remaining portion of the tax -- 0.4 percent of GDP -- was not under dispute in this latest review. Therefore the entire tax, representing 0.6 percent of GDP, can now be applied towards the 1997 budget deficit.

Regarding the treatment of state guarantees for Italy's railway system, Eurostat ruled that "public enterprises' debt guaranteed by the state should be directly taken into account in the government debt."
